cards.explanation: The answer is teaching. Jesus did not want anyone to know, because He was teaching His disciples. I think of it as a classroom on the move, with a teacher and His students walking through Galilee.

The answer is that they will kill Him. Jesus says the Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men, and "They will kill Him…" He doesn't dress it up or soften it. I think that is a heavy thing to hear on a walk.
The answer is three days. Jesus says, "…and after three days He will rise." That's the hopeful part of a very heavy sentence. He tells them both halves.

The answer is False. The disciples did not understand, and "…they were afraid to ask Him about it." Nobody raised a hand. I think we've all nodded along in a meeting at something we didn't get, then Googled it in the parking lot.
The answer is False. Jesus asks what they were discussing on the way, and the text says they were silent. Not one disciple jumped in. I bet you could've heard a cookie crumb land in that house.

The answer is that they were arguing about which of them was the greatest. When Jesus asked what they were discussing, they were silent. When a room goes quiet like that, I think they already knew what He'd say.

The answer is last. Jesus says, "If anyone wants to be first, he must be the last of all and the servant of all." They were busy arguing about who's on top, and He turned the whole ladder upside down. Servant of all is the job description here, friends.

The answer is that He takes the child in His arms. Jesus has a little child stand among them, and then He takes the child in His arms. The disciples had been arguing about who's greatest, and now they're watching Jesus hold a child. Then He tells them about welcoming one.
The answer is True. Jesus says, "…whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me." So a welcome that starts small goes a long way up. That's a lot of weight on one little welcome.
The answer is True. John, one of the disciples, tells Jesus, "…we tried to stop him…" He says it right out loud. That's a brave thing to admit to the Teacher.

The answer is that the man wasn't traveling with them. John says they tried to stop him "…because he does not accompany us." The man was driving out demons in Jesus' name, but he wasn't part of their group. In other words, he wasn't on their roster.

The answer is False. Jesus says nothing about the man joining the Twelve. He says, "Do not stop him…" and then gives His reason: "…no one who performs a miracle in My name can turn around and speak evil of Me." The joining part isn't in the text.
The answer is anyone who is not against them. Jesus says, "For whoever is not against us is for us." Short line, big door, friends.
The answer is reward. Jesus says the one who gives that cup of water "…will never lose his reward." A cup of water is not a fancy gift, friends. No big platter, no ribbon, and the reward still stays.

The answer is True, and I think this one is heavy. Jesus says if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Him to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea. Those are His words, with nothing softened.
The answer is eye. Jesus goes hand, then foot, then eye: "…if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out." Three warnings in a row, same serious tone. He doesn't soften any of them.

The answer is the kingdom of God. Jesus says it is better "…to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell…" That is His warning about an eye that causes you to sin. This is a heavy part, so I'll just say it plainly.

The answer is that it can lose its saltiness. Jesus says, "Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it?" He asks it as a question and leaves it there. And then He gives them something to do with salt.

The answers are salt and peace. Jesus says, "Have salt among yourselves…" right after talking about salt and its saltiness. Then He adds, "…and be at peace with one another." Remember, these are the same disciples who had been arguing about which of them was the greatest. His last word to them is peace.
